prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign AQUARIUS: a tall two-handled water jar (an amphora) seen from the front, standing upright in the centre. Water wells up from its mouth and pours down both sides in two matching streams that turn into bold zigzag waves at the bottom. A single small star shines above the jar.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, long zigzag waves of air and small bright stars spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. There is no face and no figure at all: only the object. The sign's nature shows only through form: even zigzag waves, clear open space, a bright unbroken flow given away freely: originality, friendship, vision, the new idea.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: ice white, electric blue, bright aqua, lemon yellow. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
